theme: Peak-summer tomatoes: a big-batch fresh sugo and a jar of sweet peperonata to carry the full-house week

components.name: Late-Summer Tomato Sugo (big batch)
components.ingredients: 5-6 lb ripe tomatoes (+ 2 cans San Marzano as backstop), 1 head garlic, big bunch basil, generous extra-virgin olive oil, salt, pinch sugar if needed
components.method: Score and blanch the tomatoes 30 sec, ice-bath, and slip off the skins (or halve and grate on a box grater, discarding skins). Warm a real glug of olive oil over medium-low and cook 6-8 smashed garlic cloves until soft and fragrant but not browned. Add the tomatoes and their juice plus the canned tomatoes crushed by hand, salt well, and simmer gently 45-60 min, stirring now and then, until jammy and glossy. Off heat, stir in torn basil and a final drizzle of oil. Cool. Makes ~7 cups; keeps 5 days fridge, freezes beautifully.

components.name: Sweet Peperonata (stewed peppers and onions)
components.ingredients: 5 red/yellow bell peppers, 2 onions, 3 garlic cloves, 2 tomatoes (or a ladle of the sugo), splash red wine vinegar, olive oil, salt
components.method: Slice peppers and onions into strips. Sweat the onions low and slow in plenty of olive oil ~10 min without browning. Add peppers, garlic, and salt; cover and cook ~15 min to soften, then uncover and let it jam down another 15-20 min. Stir in chopped tomato (or a ladle of sugo) and finish with a splash of red wine vinegar to brighten. Cool. Delicious warm or at room temp; keeps ~5 days.

dinners.name: Spaghetti al Pomodoro (the mantecatura night)
dinners.ingredients: sugo, spaghetti, reserved pasta water, extra-virgin olive oil, basil, Parmigiano
steps: Boil spaghetti in well-salted water; pull it a minute shy of al dente and save a mug of pasta water.
Warm sugo in a wide pan with a splash of olive oil.
Add the pasta and a splash of pasta water; toss hard over the heat, then off heat, adding water bit by bit until the sauce turns glossy and clings.
Finish with torn basil, grated Parmigiano, and a last drizzle of oil.
Serve kids' portions milder with extra cheese on top.

dinners.name: Baked Gnocchi al Forno
dinners.ingredients: gnocchi (or short pasta), sugo, fresh mozzarella, Parmigiano, basil, olive oil
steps: Heat oven to 425F. Boil gnocchi 2 min until they float, drain.
Toss gnocchi with plenty of warm sugo and half the torn mozzarella.
Spread in an oiled baking dish, top with remaining mozzarella and a shower of Parmigiano.
Bake 15-20 min until bubbling and browned in spots; rest 5 min.
Finish with basil and a drizzle of oil. A total kid magnet.

dinners.name: Pan-Seared Cod with Peperonata
dinners.ingredients: 6 cod (or branzino) fillets, peperonata, lemon, olive oil, crusty bread, parsley
steps: Pat fish very dry, salt it, and let sit 10 min while peperonata warms in a pan.
Sear fish skin-side or presentation-side down in hot olive oil, undisturbed, until golden; flip and finish gently.
Spoon warm peperonata onto plates and set the fish on top.
Squeeze lemon over, scatter parsley, drizzle oil, and serve with bread to mop up.
For the girls, break fish into flakes over buttered bread or plain peperonata.

dinners.name: Chicken Thighs Braised in Sugo (cacciatora-style)
dinners.ingredients: bone-in chicken thighs, sugo, peperonata, olive oil, polenta or crusty bread, Parmigiano
steps: Season thighs and brown well in olive oil, skin-side down, until crisp; remove.
Add sugo and a scoop of peperonata to the pan, nestle the thighs back in skin-up.
Simmer partially covered ~25 min until the chicken is tender and the sauce has reduced.
Meanwhile cook soft polenta (or warm bread).
Spoon chicken and sauce over polenta with grated Parmigiano; kid portions off the bone.

technique.name: Mantecatura (emulsifying pasta with its sauce)
technique.tiedTo: Spaghetti al Pomodoro - finish the pasta in the pan with sugo and starchy pasta water, tossing hard off the heat so the fat and starch emulsify into a glossy sauce that clings to every strand instead of sliding off.

shopping.items: 5-6 lb ripe tomatoes, 5 red/yellow bell peppers, 3 onions, 2 heads garlic, 2 big bunches basil, flat-leaf parsley, 2 lemons
2 balls fresh mozzarella, wedge Parmigiano-Reggiano, butter
2 cans San Marzano tomatoes, 1.5 lb spaghetti, 2 lb gnocchi (or short pasta), polenta, red wine vinegar, extra-virgin olive oil, crusty bread, salt, black pepper

scaleNote: This week is the full house (2 adults + 4 girls under 10), so all quantities above are sized for 6. Both components are kid-friendly workhorses: serve the sugo and peperonata a touch milder and put cheese, bread, and plain components on the side so the girls can customize. On the two-adult weeks, halve the batch (or freeze half the sugo), lean more technique-forward, and let the peperonata shine as a room-temp antipasto with the seared fish.
